data.name: Kailash
data.gender_notes: Kailash is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Kailash is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kailasa', which means 'the abode of Lord Shiva'. Kailash is considered as the residence of Lord Shiva, who is the supreme god of the Hindu pantheon. The name Kailash carries the meaning “Lord of the Mountain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Kailash usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Kailash is a sacred name, symbolizing the spiritual journey towards the divine. It represents the attainment of the ultimate goal of life, which is to achieve union with the supreme consciousness.
data.etymology: Kailash belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Mountain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kailash total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kailash has deep cultural significance in Hinduism as it holds a special place in Indian history and mythology. The Kailash Range in the Himalayas, which includes Mount Kailash, is renowned as a sacred pilgrimage site for Hindus, Buddhists, and Jains. Thousands of people from around the world embark on arduous journeys to trek to the remote region each year, believing that doing so would bring them closer to their deities and attain spiritual growth. The site of the majestic mountain and its circumnavigation is also a popular motif in Hindu and Buddhist arts and literature.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Kailash is revered as the ultimate abode of Lord Shiva, the god of destruction and transformation. It is believed that the mountain represents Lord Shiva and Lord Shiva resides in and within every being as the inner self, the creator of all origination and the destroyer of all destruction. Visiting Kailash is believed to bring immense blessings, spiritual awakening, and purification of the soul. The pilgrimage to Kailash is considered one of the holiest journeys in Hinduism and is said to wash away all sins. Moreover, the circumambulation of the peak symbolizes the spiritual journey of life – the constant journey towards attaining moksha (liberation of the soul) and self-realization or enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kailash, derived from Sanskrit, symbolizes the spiritual pinnacle of existence, the abode of Lord Shiva, the embodiment of transcendence and bliss. It represents the ultimate goal of spiritual journey and the realization of cosmic consciousness.

vedic_reference.note: Kailash is a sacred mountain in Hinduism and Buddhism, and is considered the residence of Lord Shiva and Parvati.

historical_references.reference: Kailash was a sacred mountain in the ancient Hindu scripture, the Mahabharata. It is said that the gods resided here and that Shiva, the god of destruction, lived on Mount Kailash.

The Tibetan Buddhists believe that Mount Kailash is the center of the universe and a sacred site of pilgrimage. It is said that the Buddha Shakyamuni visited Mount Kailash during his lifetime and that it is the place of his renunciation.

trends: Mount Kailash is a renowned pilgrimage site for Hindus, Buddhists, and Jain followers. It is located in the Ngari Prefecture of Tibet Autonomous Region, China.
modern_usage.modern_context: Mount Kailash, also known as Tangri Tibetan, is considered the holiest mountain in Hinduism and the center of the universe in Buddhism. It is a popular destination for religious tourism, attracting thousands of pilgrims every year from around the world. In social media, there are numerous posts and discussions about the spiritual significance of Mount Kailash, travel experiences, and the challenges of making the pilgrimage. The travel industry offers numerous tours and packages for people looking to visit Mount Kailash. Additionally, Mount Kailash is a significant cultural and historical site, and there is ongoing research and study of its significance in various religious and cultural contexts.
